pages.observation: The reading order is clear: a Z-path through the four upper panels, then the bottom tier. Captions sit in the top-left corners and cover no faces. Panel 2's caption box touches the top of the woman's hair but not her face. Panel 1's caption overlaps the top edge of a wall monitor, which is harmless. Ambiguities: (1) 'Ravi' is named for the first time in panel 3 with no earlier introduction, but the caption and the image make clear who he is. (2) The caption says the QR code is 'at the door', but the stand appears inside near the desk and waiting area. A glass door is visible at the right, so this is only a mild mismatch. (3) Panel 5 does not show which slot belongs to whom. The left-to-right seating suggests the elderly man is A-10, the woman A-11 and Ravi A-12, but this is inferred. (4) 'Shared with consent' is abstract, and nothing on the page shows a consent step. With no dialogue at all, the page reads as narration-led. No text is hard to read and no tails are involved.
